definitions.explanation: a type of Japanese omelet made by rolling thin layers of egg mixed with dashi broth; softer and more moist than tamagoyaki

examples.japanese: {出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご}を{作|つく}る。
{京都|きょうと}の{出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご}は{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
{出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご}はふわふわでおいしい。
examples.english: The dashimaki tamago is fluffy and delicious.

notes:
JAPANESE EGG DISHES:
{出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご} is a Kyoto-style Japanese omelet made with dashi broth, resulting in a soft, moist texture.

DIFFERENCE FROM {卵焼|たまごや}き:
- {出汁巻|だしま}き{卵|たまご}: Contains dashi, softer and juicier, more common in Kansai
- {卵焼|たまごや}き: Often sweeter, drier, more common in Kanto

COOKING TIPS:
- Uses {出汁|だし} (dashi broth) mixed with eggs
- Cooked in a rectangular pan ({卵焼|たまごや}き{器|き})
- Requires technique to roll layers while cooking

SERVING:
- Common in {居酒屋|いざかや} (izakaya)
- Part of traditional Japanese breakfast
- Often served with {大根|だいこん}おろし (grated daikon)
